claims.text: The GPS trace for this trip measures 27.18 km travelled against a booked optimal route of 21.0 km, producing a measured excess of 6.18 km (29.43% of optimal). Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass: the excess exceeds 20% of optimal, and it exceeds 0.8 km in absolute terms. The route deviation is therefore ESTABLISHED on this trip's own telemetry, whose admissibility is COMPLETE with no issues and 100% coverage, weight 1.0.

POL-RD-01 requires the threshold test to be run on the trace figure and expressly forbids citing the trip record's rounded convenience copy. I use gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 27.18 km, not trip_record.actual_distance_km = 27.2 km. The trace's own derived deviation block reports status 'established', threshold_km 0.8 and threshold_pct 20.0, so the finding does not depend on the rounded field.

The driver's own admission corroborates the deviation independently of the trace: at 10:42:05 he wrote 'sorry boss missed the exit, coming back now', and the rider's preceding message at 10:41:12 asked 'why we going towards city centre? MBS is the other side'. That is exactly the independent corroborating source a driver admission in the chat_log supplies, so the deviation is supported by two artifacts, not one.

No traffic advisory covers this trip: EV-ADVIS-00101-01 is MISSING, its weight_multiplier is 0.0, and its own issue detail records that no LTA advisory was issued for the AYE/MCE/ECP corridor in the 10:14-10:59 window on 12 July 2026. Without the advisory POL-RD-03 cannot be run at all, and the driver's own account is that he missed the exit - driver error, not an external traffic event. Under POL-RD-13 the driver's explanation is tested against the advisory and nothing else; the advisory is absent, so the explanation carries no weight. I cite the missing artifact's identifier so the absence itself is on the record.

POL-RD-04 does not exonerate any part of the excess. The clause requires a rider instruction recorded in the chat_log, timestamped before the vehicle leaves the optimal corridor, and corroborated by a waypoint_hint the platform resolved at ingest. Every message in this trip's chat_log carries waypoint_hint null and no road or place is named by the rider; the only route-relevant message is the rider querying why the car was heading towards the city centre. The corroboration test is undecidable on the record, the clause is unavailable, and none of the 6.18 km excess is excluded.

POL-RD-12 has no application here. The trip record shows vehicle_type RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so there is no matched-itinerary baseline and no co-rider collection distance to exclude. The full 6.18 km of trace excess stands measured against the booked optimal of 21.0 km.

POL-RD-11 does not shield the charge. The fare_breakdown shows fare_model METERED and quoted_fare_sgd null, so this is not an upfront-quoted trip and the distance-and-time refund route under POL-RD-02 is open and runs as written.

With the deviation established and no exculpatory clause available, the refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02 on the METERED model: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 21.0 + 0.28 x 26.0) x 1.0, the surge_multiplier read from the fare_breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = 27.63. Refund = 35.64 charged_total - 27.63 = 8.01, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 8.05. That is above the 0.50 de minimis floor and below 90% of charged_total, so the correct outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of 8.05, not FULL_REFUND. These three figures - charged_total 35.64, recomputed_fare 27.63, refund 8.05 - are stated separately as POL-RD-02 requires.

The rider discharges the POL-RD-08 initial burden: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00101 and the same pickup window on 12 July 2026, and the excess of 6.18 km meets the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The burden shifts to the driver, who must name a specific artifact and a specific clause to invoke POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-12; he names none, and an uncited traffic assertion does not discharge that burden. Separate from the burden question, the rider_profile's deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the elevated corroboration requirement for sub-30% claims is not triggered, and in any event the driver's chat admission supplies it.

The ERP and surcharge position is clean on the record and adds nothing to either side: the fare_breakdown's erp_lines are empty, off-optimal-route and on-optimal-route ERP totals are both 0.00, and the airport_surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor (for surcharge purposes) is chargeable at an airport. There is accordingly no separate pass-through or billing-integrity correction to stack on top of the POL-RD-02 refund, and the 8.05 refund stands as the whole of the money the rider is owed.

claims.text: The divergence is real but modest, and it is not a material one. The GPS trace's derived excess is 6.18 km over a 21.0 km optimal route, 29.43%, which clears the POL-RD-01 establishment gate (greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km) yet falls short of both MATERIAL thresholds (greater than 50% and greater than 8.0 km). This is a non-material, partial-excess deviation, and the aggravated machinery reserved for material deviations does not attach.

No repeat-deviation pattern is established, so the driver is treated as this single trip shows him. On the only counters POL-RD-06 permits for this test, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 812, giving a ratio of 0.0 against the 0.05 threshold and a raw counter below 3. The clause's three consequences therefore cannot fire: no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) and no driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c). POL-GEN-01 confines the test to those two fields alone.

The remedy is the POL-RD-02 arithmetic and nothing beyond it. This is a METERED fare, so recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 21.0 + 0.28 x 26.0) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee = 27.63; refund = charged_total 35.64 less 27.63 = 8.01, payable rounded UP to 8.05, with no intermediate rounding. The rider's own anchor in her claim, 'about 21km and around $27', in fact matches the 27.63 recomputed fare, and the 10.00 she contests is some 1.95 more than the policy provides.

Nothing may be added on top of that figure. erp_lines total is 0.00, there are no off-optimal-route gantries and no off-route ERP, so POL-RD-09(1)'s anti-double-count rule leaves the distance-and-time refund exactly as computed. Equally no charge line fails the billing-integrity test: the base, distance, time and platform lines reconcile to the 35.64 charged_total, erp_gantries is empty and airport_surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that does not originate at an airport, so no standalone POL-RD-09(4) correction and no billing-integrity referral attaches to this driver.

No exculpatory clause is available and none is needed to bound the outcome. The only traffic_advisory for this corridor is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so POL-RD-03 cannot be run; the chat log carries no rider instruction to detour, the trip_record shows no pickup or dropoff amendment, and vehicle_type is RYDE_X rather than RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 and POL-RD-12 are all off the table. The GPS trace is COMPLETE at 100% coverage with no gaps, so POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10 have no impaired-trace or missing-corroboration trigger. Under POL-RD-13(2) the deviation therefore stands at the measured figure and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal: the case ends in a bounded partial refund, not a full refund and not an escalation.

The GPS trace for trip TRP-00101 measures 27.18 km against the booked optimal route of 21.0 km, an excess of 6.18 km, or 29.43% of optimal. That clears both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km), so the deviation is established on this trip's own telemetry. The governing measurement is the trace figure of 27.18 km, not the trip record's rounded 27.2 km, as POL-RD-01 requires. The driver's own chat message at 10:42:05 - 'sorry boss missed the exit, coming back now' - is an admission against his own interest and independently confirms the deviation, so the finding does not rest on the trace alone. The deviation is not MATERIAL: it is under both the 50% and the 8.0 km materiality thresholds, so the POL-RD-06 machinery does not attach. His profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 against 812 completed trips in 90 days, which establishes no repeat pattern, and no driver-conduct referral follows. The refund is 35.64 less 27.63 = 8.01, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05, which is 8.05. That is above the 0.50 de minimis floor and well below 90% of charged_total, so the outcome is a partial refund. The 10.00 you contested is not payable; the policy provides 8.05. To the driver: no exculpatory route is open on this record. No traffic advisory exists for this trip - EV-ADVIS-00101-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 - so POL-RD-03 cannot be run, and you asserted no external traffic cause in any event; your own account is driver error. The chat log carries no rider instruction to detour, and every waypoint_hint is null, so POL-RD-04 does not exonerate any part of the excess. The trip record shows no pickup or dropoff amendment, so POL-RD-05 is off the table, and the vehicle was RYDE_X rather than RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply. The fare was METERED with no upfront quote, so POL-RD-11 does not shield the charge. All ERP and surcharge lines are 0.00 and all fare lines reconcile to the 35.64 charged, so there is no pass-through or billing-integrity correction and no referral. Finally, the trace is COMPLETE at 100% coverage with no gaps, so POL-RD-07 and the POL-RD-10 escalation triggers do not fire; the ruling is a bounded PARTIAL_REFUND of 8.05 with no amount held.

ruling.explanation:
This ruling is addressed to both parties.

FINDINGS. The route deviation is established on this trip's own telemetry. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00101, admissibility COMPLETE, weight 1.0, 100% coverage, no gaps) measures 27.18 km against the booked optimal of 21.0 km on the trip record (EV-TRIP-00101), an excess of 6.18 km, which is 29.43% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass: the excess exceeds 20% of optimal and exceeds 0.8 km in absolute terms. As POL-RD-01 requires, I used the trace figure (27.18 km), not the trip record's rounded copy (27.2 km). The deviation is not a MATERIAL one: 29.43% is below the 50% material threshold and 6.18 km is below the 8.0 km material threshold, so the aggravated machinery does not attach.

EXCULPATION. No exoneration applies. POL-RD-03 cannot be run: the only traffic advisory for this corridor, EV-ADVIS-00101-01, is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so there is no advisory naming a traversed segment with an overlapping validity window. In any event the driver's own messages say he "missed the exit" - driver error, not an external traffic event; a missing advisory is a gap in the bundle here, not a POL-RD-10(5) contradiction, and it does not escalate the case. POL-RD-04 is unavailable: the chat log (EV-CHAT-00101) carries no rider instruction to detour, every message has waypoint_hint null, and the rider's only route message asks why the car was heading the wrong way, so the corroboration test cannot run and no distance is excluded. POL-RD-05 does not apply (no pickup or dropoff amendment). POL-RD-12 does not apply (vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL). POL-RD-11 does not apply (fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so this is not an upfront-quoted trip).

REMEDY (POL-RD-02), stated on separate lines as the clause requires. charged_total = 35.64. recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 21.0 optimal km + 0.28 x 26.0 optimal min) x 1.0 surge_multiplier read from the fare_breakdown (EV-FARE-00101) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP/tolls = 27.63. Refund = 35.64 - 27.63 = 8.01, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 8.05. That is above the 0.50 de minimis floor and well below 90% of charged_total, so this is a PARTIAL_REFUND of 8.05, not a full refund.

ON THE CLAIMS. The rider asked for the $10.00 difference she calculated; the policy provides 8.05, and her own anchor of "about 21km and around $27" matches the recomputed fare of 27.63. Her point that the driver admitted missing the exit is accepted (his message at 10:42:05, and his written counterparty statement, both concede it), and it corroborates the trace, but it does not enlarge the remedy beyond the arithmetic the policy sets. The driver's points are also accepted: the deviation is non-material; POL-RD-09 adds nothing because erp_lines are empty (both on-optimal and off-optimal totals 0.00) and the airport surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that does not originate at an airport, so there is no separate pass-through or billing-integrity correction to stack on the 8.05. On POL-RD-06, using only the fields the clause permits, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 812 (ratio 0.0, below 0.05), so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and neither the POL-RD-06(b) full-refund uplift nor the POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral fires. No billing-integrity referral under POL-RD-09(4) fires either, since every charge line reconciles to the 35.64 total.

CONFIDENCE AND RECORD. Confidence is capped by the weight of the artifacts carrying the deciding facts, all of which are weight 1.0 (GPS trace, trip record, fare breakdown); the capped confidence is therefore 0.95. The one missing artifact, EV-ADVIS-00101-01, carries nothing and is not relied on. One advocate claim was discarded at the mechanical stage and is recorded below; the rider's separate submission about the absent advisory, phrased as an exculpatory-clause point, is answered here: the advisory's absence is noted on the record and does not change the outcome. The driver's charge stands except for the distance-and-time refund of 8.05.

ledger.claim: POL-RD-04 does not exonerate any part of the excess. The clause requires a rider instruction recorded in the chat_log, timestamped before the vehicle leaves the optimal corridor, and corroborated by a waypoint_hint the platform resolved at ingest. Every message in this trip's chat_log carries waypoint_hint null and no road or place is named by the rider; the only route-relevant message is the rider querying why the car was heading towards the city centre. The corroboration test is undecidable on the record, the clause is unavailable, and none of the 6.18 km excess is excluded.

POL-RD-12 has no application here. The trip record shows vehicle_type RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so there is no matched-itinerary baseline and no co-rider collection distance to exclude. The full 6.18 km of trace excess stands measured against the booked optimal of 21.0 km.

POL-RD-11 does not shield the charge. The fare_breakdown shows fare_model METERED and quoted_fare_sgd null, so this is not an upfront-quoted trip and the distance-and-time refund route under POL-RD-02 is open and runs as written.

With the deviation established and no exculpatory clause available, the refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02 on the METERED model: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 21.0 + 0.28 x 26.0) x 1.0, the surge_multiplier read from the fare_breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = 27.63. Refund = 35.64 charged_total - 27.63 = 8.01, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 8.05. That is above the 0.50 de minimis floor and below 90% of charged_total, so the correct outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of 8.05, not FULL_REFUND. These three figures - charged_total 35.64, recomputed_fare 27.63, refund 8.05 - are stated separately as POL-RD-02 requires.

The rider discharges the POL-RD-08 initial burden: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00101 and the same pickup window on 12 July 2026, and the excess of 6.18 km meets the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The burden shifts to the driver, who must name a specific artifact and a specific clause to invoke POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-12; he names none, and an uncited traffic assertion does not discharge that burden. Separate from the burden question, the rider_profile's deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the elevated corroboration requirement for sub-30% claims is not triggered, and in any event the driver's chat admission supplies it.

The ERP and surcharge position is clean on the record and adds nothing to either side: the fare_breakdown's erp_lines are empty, off-optimal-route and on-optimal-route ERP totals are both 0.00, and the airport_surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor (for surcharge purposes) is chargeable at an airport. There is accordingly no separate pass-through or billing-integrity correction to stack on top of the POL-RD-02 refund, and the 8.05 refund stands as the whole of the money the rider is owed.

The divergence is real but modest, and it is not a material one. The GPS trace's derived excess is 6.18 km over a 21.0 km optimal route, 29.43%, which clears the POL-RD-01 establishment gate (greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km) yet falls short of both MATERIAL thresholds (greater than 50% and greater than 8.0 km). This is a non-material, partial-excess deviation, and the aggravated machinery reserved for material deviations does not attach.

No repeat-deviation pattern is established, so the driver is treated as this single trip shows him. On the only counters POL-RD-06 permits for this test, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 812, giving a ratio of 0.0 against the 0.05 threshold and a raw counter below 3. The clause's three consequences therefore cannot fire: no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) and no driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c). POL-GEN-01 confines the test to those two fields alone.

The remedy is the POL-RD-02 arithmetic and nothing beyond it. This is a METERED fare, so recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 21.0 + 0.28 x 26.0) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee = 27.63; refund = charged_total 35.64 less 27.63 = 8.01, payable rounded UP to 8.05, with no intermediate rounding. The rider's own anchor in her claim, 'about 21km and around $27', in fact matches the 27.63 recomputed fare, and the 10.00 she contests is some 1.95 more than the policy provides.

Nothing may be added on top of that figure. erp_lines total is 0.00, there are no off-optimal-route gantries and no off-route ERP, so POL-RD-09(1)'s anti-double-count rule leaves the distance-and-time refund exactly as computed. Equally no charge line fails the billing-integrity test: the base, distance, time and platform lines reconcile to the 35.64 charged_total, erp_gantries is empty and airport_surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that does not originate at an airport, so no standalone POL-RD-09(4) correction and no billing-integrity referral attaches to this driver.

No exculpatory clause is available and none is needed to bound the outcome. The only traffic_advisory for this corridor is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so POL-RD-03 cannot be run; the chat log carries no rider instruction to detour, the trip_record shows no pickup or dropoff amendment, and vehicle_type is RYDE_X rather than RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 and POL-RD-12 are all off the table. The GPS trace is COMPLETE at 100% coverage with no gaps, so POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10 have no impaired-trace or missing-corroboration trigger. Under POL-RD-13(2) the deviation therefore stands at the measured figure and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal: the case ends in a bounded partial refund, not a full refund and not an escalation.
